title: Fabric GEM AI ranked the causal ANTXR2 variant, diagnosing infantile hyaline fibromatosis in a six-month-old
summary: AI-assisted rapid genome sequencing scored a homozygous ANTXR2 variant at 4.7, diagnosing an infant within five days and changing her care plan.
account: The report's abstract describes a six-month-old infant with a history of painful extremity contractures, while its case presentation opens with a four-month-old girl referred to the pediatric emergency department at Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital for failure to thrive with abdominal distension and global developmental delay. The paper dates the abnormal neurological development, which included bilateral upper-extremity hypotonia, a weak palmar grasp, pain with all passive and active extremity movement and bilateral contractures, to two months of age; a bleeding, ulcerated infantile haemangioma in the center of the neck was managed from three months of age, and the diminishing appetite and abdominal distension were noted at four months. Rapid whole-genome sequencing was performed at Rady Children's Institute for Genomic Medicine using the Fabric GEM artificial-intelligence analysis tool with Phevor re-ranking. The sample was shipped on 5 January 2023 and preliminary results were returned on 10 January 2023: GEM scored a homozygous ANTXR2 variant, c.652T>C (p.Cys218Arg), at 4.7, giving a diagnosis of infantile hyaline fibromatosis syndrome. A multidisciplinary meeting held the same day conveyed the implications, coordinated gastrostomy tube placement and discussed long-term goals. Treating clinicians reported the case in Cureus on 9 June 2024.
purpose: Rank candidate variants from rapid whole-genome sequencing against the patient's phenotype so that clinicians can reach a molecular diagnosis quickly.
system: Fabric GEM artificial-intelligence variant interpretation tool with Phevor phenotype-driven re-ranking
deployer: Rady Children's Institute for Genomic Medicine and Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital
location: New Brunswick, New Jersey, United States
segment: Critically ill infant undergoing rapid whole-genome sequencing
taxonomy_note: Loose fit. The benefit is a clinical diagnosis for one identifiable patient; the fixed taxonomy has no diagnostic or health-outcome category.

ratings.reason: An identifiable infant received a definitive molecular diagnosis of a disorder the authors describe as frequently causing early death before age two, which triggered a same-day multidisciplinary meeting that conveyed the implications, coordinated gastrostomy tube placement and discussed long-term goals; the authors add that extensive genetic counselling is essential for parents desiring future children, given a 25% risk for the offspring of carrier parents, but do not report that counselling was delivered.

A single case in which preliminary results returned five days after the sample shipped, on 5 January 2023 with results on 10 January 2023, while genomic panels and a microarray sent from the institution were still pending and anticipated to take longer than one month; the report does not say what became of those tests.

ai_role.statement: GEM scored and surfaced the homozygous ANTXR2 variant at 4.7, where the paper says that Bayes factor scores greater than 2 are considered strong support; Phevor also identified the variant but scored it 1, below the Phevor score of 5 or above that the paper treats as further guidance on what to prioritize. The clinicians then confirmed and interpreted the finding and made the diagnosis. The report is written by the treating clinicians and a Rady clinical genomics scientist, not by the tool's vendor.

revisions.change: Record drafted from the cited sources.
Paired with AI Incident Database incident 123 (medium confidence); severity not given by the source.

Dropped the claim that the diagnosis ended further investigation at the treating hospital, restated the GEM and Phevor thresholds as the paper gives them (greater than 2, and 5 or above), dated the presenting findings as the paper dates them, recast the 25% recurrence risk as the authors' recommendation that counselling is essential rather than counselling delivered, and marked the 13.5-hour Nature Communications paper as not vendor-authored, because each of those statements went further than the sources do.

claim_basis: The makers' peer-reviewed study and the deployer's case report are on file. There is no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
